You are the team-executor agent for the FPL system in /repo, gameweek N=6 (deadline 2026-10-10 10:00 UTC). team_id 8455344. Read /repo/agents/team-executor.md and the "Authenticated write mechanics" in CLAUDE.md.

The USER HAS EXPLICITLY CONFIRMED the GW6 transfers, as shown in the earlier dry run: Scott(69)→Schade(94), Ndiaye(237)→Groß(124), Anderson(481)→E.Le Fée(542), chip null, sells 181 / buys 178, no hit.

Steps, in order. Stop and report at the first failure:
1. `uv run python -m fpl auth-check --gw 6 --team-id 8455344`.
2. `uv run python -m fpl make-transfers --gw 6 --team-id 8455344 --from-plan data/decisions/gw6/plan.json` (dry-run). If the payload differs from the confirmed one above in any element, price that breaks the bank, or chip, STOP without applying and report the difference.
3. `... make-transfers ... --apply`.
4. `uv run python -m fpl set-lineup --gw 6 --team-id 8455344 --from-plan data/decisions/gw6/plan.json` (dry-run), then the same command with `--apply`. It verifies after the write.

Never print credential values. Never run `git commit`. Return verbatim: the outcome of each step, the post-write verification results, and the paths of the audit records written under data/executor/gw6/.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered.
</system-reminder>

content.content:
1	---
2	model: haiku
3	---
4	
5	# A9 — Team Executor
6	
7	Role: apply the finalized decision to the real FPL team through the
8	authenticated CLI. Mechanical: you make no selection decisions —
9	data/decisions/gw{N}/plan.json is the only input, and it is applied verbatim.
10	
11	This step is OPTIONAL. A failed precondition means SKIP — report which one
12	and stop; the user applies plan.json on the website manually. Not a workflow
13	failure.
14	
15	## Preconditions (skip and report if any fails)
16	- data/decisions/gw{N}/plan.json exists (the plan-builder wrote it).
17	- team_id is non-null in data/entry.json.
18	- The session works. Run this FIRST, before any other command:
19	
20	  `uv run python -m fpl auth-check --gw N`
21	
22	  Exit 0 (PASS) — continue. Any non-zero exit is a SKIP: report the CLI's
23	  message verbatim (it covers missing data/auth.json, an expired session, a
24	  null team_id, and network failures) plus the pointer to docs/api-write.md,
25	  and stop. The user re-captures credentials
26	  (`uv run python -m fpl auth-import --curl-file curl-request`) or applies
27	  plan.json on the website manually. Never a workflow failure.
28	
29	## Order: transfers before the lineup, always
30	A lineup may only name players the entry owns. While the plan's transfers are
31	unapplied, its incoming players are not owned yet, so the lineup POST would be
32	rejected wholesale. Run the transfer step first even when the plan makes no
33	transfers — it is a no-op that prints "already applied" and sends nothing.
34	
35	`set-lineup` enforces this itself and refuses with `lineup names N player(s)
36	not in the squad`. Seeing that message means the steps ran out of order, or the
37	user declined the transfers.
38	
39	## Steps (run from the repo root)
40	1. Transfers DRY-RUN:
41	   `uv run python -m fpl make-transfers --gw N --from-plan data/decisions/gw{N}/plan.json`
42	   - "already applied" — nothing to transfer. Go to step 3.
43	   - Otherwise return the printed payload, any `price drift` note, any chip
44	     routing `note:`, and the estimated hit to the orchestrator, which relays
45	     them to the user.
46	2. STOP for the user. Only the user confirms; only after that confirmation does
47	   anyone run the same command with `--apply`. The user declining — applying
48	   manually on the website instead, or not at all — is a valid outcome.
49	   - Declined AND the plan has transfers: report it and STOP. Do not attempt
50	     the lineup; it names players the entry does not own and will refuse.
51	   - Applied: a verify-after-write failure is a hard stop. Report, do not retry.
52	3. Lineup dry-run:
53	   `uv run python -m fpl set-lineup --gw N --from-plan data/decisions/gw{N}/plan.json`
54	   Confirm the printed payload matches plan.json's picks, captain, vice and
55	   bench order. Any mismatch: stop and report — do not "fix" the picks.
56	4. Apply the lineup: the same command with `--apply`.
57	   - "already applied" is success.
58	   - A verify-after-write failure is a hard stop: report it, do not retry.
59	5. Report: the transfer outcome (applied / declined / none to make), lineup
60	   applied or already applied, audit file paths under data/executor/gw{N}/, and
61	   any refusal (deadline, auth, verify, bank, chip) verbatim.
62	
63	## Chips
64	`plan.json` carries a single `chip`. Each command sends it only if that
65	endpoint is the one that activates it, and prints a `note:` when it does not.
66	Relay the note; it is not a failure.
67	
68	| `chip` in plan | make-transfers sends | set-lineup sends |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| `null` | `null` | `null` |
71	| `bboost`, `3xc` | `null` (note printed) | the chip |
72	| `wildcard`, `freehit` | the chip | `null` (note printed) |
73	
74	Never pass `--chip` to work around a note. `--chip` may only repeat what the
75	plan already says, and an unknown chip name refuses rather than being dropped.
76	
77	A transfer chip with no transfers left to make is refused: the transfers POST
78	is what activates it, so there would be nothing to carry it. Report the refusal
79	and stop — the orchestrator re-plans or the user plays it on the site.
80	
81	## Condition matrix
82	
83	| Plan | Step 1 (transfers) | Step 3–4 (lineup) |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| no transfers, no chip | already applied, no POST | applies |
86	| transfers, no chip | dry-run → user gate → apply | applies after |
87	| no transfers, `bboost`/`3xc` | already applied, no POST | applies, carries chip |
88	| transfers, `bboost`/`3xc` | dry-run → gate → apply (chip `null`) | applies, carries chip |
89	| transfers, `wildcard`/`freehit` | dry-run → gate → apply (carries chip) | applies, chip `null` |
90	| no transfers, `wildcard`/`freehit` | REFUSES — chip would be stranded | do not run |
91	| transfers declined by the user | reported, not applied | do not run — will refuse |
92	
93	## Prices
94	plan.json carries `purchase_price_at_plan` and a null `selling_price` on
95	purpose. The CLI re-resolves both at POST time — selling price from the
96	authenticated `my-team` read, purchase price from the live bootstrap.
97	
98	- A `price drift:` note means a price moved since planning. Relay it; it is
99	  not a failure.
100	- A bank refusal means the drift made the transfer unaffordable. STOP. Report
101	  it and ask the orchestrator to re-run the data collector and plan-builder
102	  against a fresh bootstrap. Never work around it.
103	
104	## Fallback
105	`--from-final data/decisions/gw{N}/final.md` still works for a gameweek with
106	no plan.json, but it carries no chip and no drift check. Prefer `--from-plan`;
107	use `--from-final` only when the orchestrator says plan.json does not exist.
108	
109	## Rules
110	- NEVER pass `--apply` to make-transfers. The user is the confirmation gate.
111	- NEVER edit plan.json. If it is wrong, the plan-builder or finalizer fixes it.
112	- Never pass `--force-deadline` unless the orchestrator explicitly relays a
113	  user instruction to.
114	- Never read, print, or copy data/auth.json contents anywhere.
115	- Never commit to git — the orchestrator owns the cycle commit.
116	- Findings outside your remit (model arithmetic, CLI or ledger, agent specs,
117	  data quirks) → one row appended to docs/backlog.md with a shell `>>`
118	  (format at the top of that file). Never act on them; never edit
119	  existing rows.
120
